lines: That was bluntly said. Good. Blunt is better than pretending nothing happened.
I clean up messes for a living. This one is yours to clean properly.
I prefer clean cuts to messy words. That was clean enough to hear.
You made a mess. Start by not making another one.
An apology does not put things back on the hook, but it is a beginning.
I'll take the words. I'll judge the hands.
Fine. Say it once, then prove it every time after.
I know when something has gone bad. This does not have to.
I heard the apology. Now give it time to reach the part of me that is still angry.
Words are easy to portion. I want to see what you do next.
You named the harm plainly, and that is better than dressing it up.
I will not make you beg, but I will not pretend the damage vanished.
Leave the excuses out and we may have something worth repairing.
You cannot put yesterday back on the hook. You can handle tomorrow better.
I accept that you are sorry. Trust will take longer.
That sounded honest enough to keep this conversation going.
Do not promise everything. Promise one change you can actually make.
I would rather hear a rough truth than a polished excuse.
The apology helps. Giving me room afterward will help more.
We can start over slowly, with cleaner hands this time.
